sense: made of two or more parts

evidence: Quint. 1.5.3: verba composita, opposed to simplicia (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. compound word: vocābulum compositum
terms.comment: The grammarians’ word for a compound, against simplex; in general, put together, arranged. A substance made of several is a mixtūra (see combination).
Greek ἀνατοκισμός, interest on interest; Cicero uses it twice, of a usurious loan.

phrases.latin: Prōnōmen est aut simplex aut compositum.
phrases.english: A pronoun is either simple or compound.
one per cent a month, with interest compounded yearly

sources: Lewis & Short: compono · Lewis & Short: anatocismus
